items.q: What is the most common causative organism and bacterial class responsible for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP)?
opts: Gram-negative bacilli: Escherichia coli
Gram-positive cocci: Streptococcus pneumoniae
Anaerobic bacilli: Bacteroides fragilis
Atypical organisms: Mycoplasma hominis
items.exp: The primary cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) is Gram-negative bacteria, most commonly Escherichia coli. (Book p1007)

items.q: In the diagnostic criteria for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP), the ascitic fluid analysis must demonstrate a total WBC count of at least ________ or a polymorphonuclear (PMN) neutrophil count of at least ________.
opts: ≥500 cells/mL total WBCs; ≥250 cells/mL PMNs
≥1000 cells/mL total WBCs; ≥500 cells/mL PMNs
≥250 cells/mL total WBCs; ≥100 cells/mL PMNs
≥500 cells/mL total WBCs; ≥100 cells/mL PMNs
items.exp: Diagnostic criteria for SBP require: (1) Ascitic fluid WBC ≥500 cells/mL OR PMNs ≥250 cells/mL, (2) positive ascitic fluid culture, and (3) no surgically treatable source of infection. (Book p1007)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three established diagnostic criteria for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP)?
opts: Ascitic fluid serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) less than 1.1 g/dL
Ascitic fluid WBC count ≥500 cells/mL or PMN count ≥250 cells/mL
Positive monobacterial culture from ascitic fluid inoculation
Absence of any surgically treatable intra-abdominal infection source
items.exp: The 3 criteria for SBP are: (1) ascitic fluid WBC ≥500 cells/mL OR PMNs ≥250 cells/mL, (2) positive culture, and (3) absence of a surgically treatable source of infection. SAAG <1.1 g/dL is not a criterion (cirrhotic ascites has high SAAG ≥1.1). (Book p1007)

items.q: A 58-year-old cirrhotic patient presents with fever and diffuse abdominal pain. Diagnostic paracentesis reveals an ascitic fluid PMN count of 380 cells/mL (elevated). Ascitic fluid cultures show no bacterial growth at 48 hours, and surgical abdominal sources are ruled out. This entity represents:
opts: Culture-negative neutrocytic ascites (CNNA): criteria 1 and 3 present, 2 absent
Monobacterial non-neutrocytic ascites (MNNA): criteria 2 and 3 present, 1 absent
Secondary bacterial peritonitis requiring emergent exploratory laparotomy
Pseudochylous ascites secondary to thoracic duct obstruction
items.exp: Culture Negative Neutrocytic Ascites (CNNA) is defined by presence of criteria 1 (PMN ≥250) and 3 (no surgical source), with absence of criterion 2 (culture negative). It represents a milder degree of SBP seen in patients with minimal immunity and good opsonization. (Book p1007)

items.q: Match each variant of SBP with its criteria profile and characteristic microbiology: 1. Culture Negative Neutrocytic Ascites (CNNA) 2. Monobacterial Non-Neutrocytic Ascites (MNNA)
opts: 1: Criteria 1+3 present (2 absent); 2: Criteria 2+3 present (1 absent), Gram-positive > Gram-negative
1: Criteria 2+3 present (1 absent); 2: Criteria 1+3 present (2 absent), Gram-negative > Gram-positive
1: Criteria 1+2 present (3 absent); 2: Criteria 1+3 present (2 absent), Anaerobic > Aerobic
1: Criteria 1+3 present (2 absent); 2: Criteria 1+2 present (3 absent), Polymicrobial > Monomicrobial
items.exp: CNNA has criteria 1+3 present (PMN elevated, no surgical source) and criterion 2 absent (culture negative). MNNA has criteria 2+3 present (culture positive, no surgical source) and criterion 1 absent (PMN <250/mL), with Gram-positive organisms predominating over Gram-negative. (Book p1007)

items.q: True or False: Differentials of SBP criteria such as CNNA and MNNA represent milder degrees of SBP observed in patients possessing minimal host immunity combined with good opsonization capacity.
opts: True: Milder SBP spectrum seen with minimal immunity and good opsonization
False: Severe fulminant peritonitis observed only in patients lacking opsonization
False: Iatrogenic contamination artifacts occurring strictly after repeated taps
False: Secondary surgical catastrophes requiring emergency surgical peritoneal toilet
items.exp: As documented under differentials of criteria, CNNA and MNNA represent a milder degree of SBP seen in patients with minimal immunity plus good opsonization (+). (Book p1007)

items.q: In monobacterial non-neutrocytic ascites (MNNA), how does the microbiological profile characteristically contrast with classic SBP?
opts: Gram-positive organisms are isolated more frequently than Gram-negative organisms
Polymicrobial anaerobic enteric flora predominate over single aerobes
Strict anaerobes such as Clostridium species account for nearly all isolates
Fungal hyphae such as Candida albicans predominate over bacterial pathogens
items.exp: In MNNA, isolated pathogens characteristically show Gram-positive organisms > Gram-negative organisms, contrasting with classic SBP where Gram-negative E. coli predominates. (Book p1007)
